newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown forecast 1997/98 PSBR of 13.25 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown forecast 1997/98 PSBR of 13.25 bln stg.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown forecast the public sector borrowing requirement would be 13.25 billion stg in fiscal 1997-98, down from 23 billion stg in 1996-97.
Brown forecast the deficit for 1998-99 would be 5.5 billion stg.

"Borrowing was projected in the last budget to be 19.25 billion stg for this year but is now set to be 13.25 billion stg," Brown told parliament. "And borrowing that was projected to be 12.25 billion stg next year is now set to be 5.5 billion."
Brown confirmed the control totals for public spending set in the last budget would be adhered to for two years.

Analysts have expressed some concern that Britain is not yet posting a surplus, despite six years of economic recovery, and that Labour is still some way from hitting its "golden rule" of only borrowing to finance investment -- around one percent of GDP.

"Beyond these years, I am publishing a range of projections based on different assumptions for spending. In every case, we meet the golden rule, see debt falling as a proportion of GDP and, because of our discipline, we go below the borrowing projections of the previous government," Brown said.
"And for this year and the foreseeable future we are comfortably within the Maastricht Criteria for levels of both debt and borrowing," he said.
